beats.text: Why does everything start on a Monday?
Google searches for diet spike at the start of every week, every month, and every year.
Students hit the gym more at the start of a week, a new semester, and right after their birthday.
It's called the fresh start effect.
A new date feels like a new chapter. Old slip-ups feel like they belong to the last one.
And it works on demand. Calling a day the first day of spring made people more likely to start.
So missed Monday? Find another first day.

sources: Dai, Milkman & Riis (2014). The fresh start effect: Temporal landmarks motivate aspirational behavior. Management Science 60(10). Google searches for 'diet' rose at the start of weeks, months, years and after holidays; university gym visits rose at the start of a week, month, semester and after birthdays.

Dai, Milkman & Riis (2015). Put your imperfections behind you: Temporal landmarks spur goal initiation when they signal new beginnings. Psychological Science 26(12). Framing March 20 as 'the first day of spring' raised reminder sign-ups (26% vs 7%). Via APS 'Minds for Business'.
